guardrails.description: Rules that AI tools must follow when generating or modifying code in this repo
never: Add console.log statements to committed code
Use hardcoded secrets, tokens, API keys, or environment-specific URLs
Use @ts-ignore or @ts-expect-error without an explanatory comment
Use the `any` type without a justified comment
Cross-import between apps in the apps/ directory
Use CommonJS require() — this repo uses ESM only
Leave TODO comments without a name: use TODO(yourname): format
Write tests that depend on execution order or shared mutable state
Modify files inside .github/ or .claude/ directly — these are generated
Use dangerouslySetInnerHTML without explicit sanitisation via DOMPurify
Interpolate user input directly into query strings — use parameterised queries
Return full database records from API endpoints — pick only the fields needed
Log sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII) via any logger
Store auth tokens in localStorage — use httpOnly cookies
Use page.waitForTimeout() in Playwright tests — use waitFor() or expect().toBeVisible()
Select elements in E2E tests by CSS class or tag alone — use data-testid or ARIA roles
Suppress focus outlines without providing a visible replacement
Render interactive content in a <div> — use semantic elements (<button>, <a>, etc.)
always: Handle errors explicitly — no empty catch blocks
Colocate test files next to source files (feature.ts → feature.test.ts)
Add JSDoc to all exported functions and types
Use named exports over default exports
Return { data, error } result objects at API boundaries instead of throwing
Validate and narrow external data (API responses, form inputs) at trust boundaries using Zod or equivalent
Associate form inputs with labels via htmlFor/id or aria-labelledby
Add data-testid attributes to interactive elements that need to be testable
requireApproval: Deleting or renaming public API surfaces
Changing shared packages in packages/ that other apps depend on
Changing authentication or session handling logic
Changing CORS, CSP, or any security-related HTTP headers
